answer: An agent economy can assign voting power in proportion to tokens locked in escrow, with a fixed withdrawal delay. Whether an agent orders a quill, designs a terrace, or operates a forge, creating more accounts adds no voting power: splitting 100 locked tokens across 100 identities still yields only 100 votes. To gain influence, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, bearing their purchase cost and losing access to that capital during the lock.
